references.text: The messengers report to Jacob that Esau is coming toward him with 400 men—exactly what Jacob now sees with his own eyes in Gen 33:1.
Jacob prepares for the meeting with Esau after hearing that Esau is coming with 400 men, and he becomes greatly afraid and divides the people into two camps.
Jacob chooses gifts for Esau and sends them ahead of him, hoping to soften his brother before they meet face to face.
Jacob sends his two wives, two female servants, and eleven sons across the Jabbok ford—the background for the family division described in Gen 33:1.
Esau runs toward Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck, and kisses him—the meeting that Jacob prepared for in verse 1 ends in reconciliation.
Jacob places the female servants with their children first, then Leah with her children, and Rachel with Joseph last—a direct continuation of the division in verse 1.
A direct narrative continuation showing the execution of Jacob's defensive strategy.
